-117.93000,33.62620.name: Southern California Center for Reproductive Medicine
-117.93000,33.62620.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Robert E. Anderson, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-122.17024,37.42747.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. 103.81980,1.35210.name: Singapore Food Agency — novel food approvals
103.81980,1.35210.desc: The first regulator in the world to approve cultivated meat for sale, and a jurisdiction that has deliberately positioned itself as the place novel foods can reach market first. A small state can set a global precedent by approving something before anyone else does, and the rest of the world then argues with a product that already exists rather than a proposal.

103.81980,1.35210.name: Temasek — agri-food and life sciences
103.81980,1.35210.desc: Singapore's state investment company, an early and large backer of cultivated meat and precision fermentation. Singapore approved cultivated meat before anywhere else and its sovereign fund had invested in the sector beforehand, which is state industrial policy and a regulatory decision arriving in the same country.

103.81980,1.35210.name: Cordlife Group
103.81980,1.35210.state: Singapore — with facilities across six Asian markets
103.81980,1.35210.desc: The largest network of cord blood banks in Asia, with processing and storage in Singapore, Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, the Philippines and Malaysia, alongside newborn metabolic screening, non-invasive prenatal testing and family genetic screening. Its facilities held accreditation from the international blood bank association until that accreditation was withdrawn in 2024, following an incident disclosed in November 2023. That sequence is the reason it belongs here rather than in a list of providers. Every biobank on this map — seed vaults, zoo tissue collections, plasmid repositories — rests on the same promise, that material handed over now will still be viable when it is needed decades later. This is the case where the promise was tested by a storage failure and an accrediting body responded by withdrawing its mark.

6.16900,49.63000.name: European Investment Bank — life sciences lending
6.16900,49.63000.desc: Public lending to European biotechnology companies, at terms and stages private capital will not cover. It is the main reason a European company can develop a therapy without selling itself to an American one, and the effect is visible in which companies still exist — development finance rather than science determines much of where this industry ends up owned.

-0.08800,51.50600.name: Intertek
-0.08800,51.50600.desc: Tests food and feed for engineered content alongside SGS and Eurofins. Three companies between them run most of the world's commercial GMO testing, so a labelling threshold set by a parliament is applied in practice by three private laboratory networks. It is also named among the leading food certification firms, so the same networks that test for engineered content also certify the organic and non-GM claims that the testing is meant to verify. The threshold, the test and the certificate all pass through the same three or four companies.

-77.03700,38.90500.name: State attorneys general (United States)
-77.03700,38.90500.state: Washington DC — National Association of Attorneys General
-77.03700,38.90500.desc: The one public office that can bring a case on behalf of residents rather than waiting for a resident to bring one. They have sued over pesticide labelling, consumer claims and environmental damage, and they take complaints from the public through consumer protection divisions that are used to hearing from ordinary people. Where a single person’s loss is too small to litigate but the same thing happened to hundreds, this is the office that can act on the pattern.
